findings.finding: Wiring a new HARD-severity gate into `run_all_checks` with no dry-run of the existing corpus. The check fires on behavior-change iterates against FRs whose `required_layers` bindings were authored before this rule existed. If any active FR has integration/E2E passing evidence but a unit-only binding, the very next behavior-touching iterate goes HARD and blocks work — potentially across the whole campaign — until bindings are manually updated. The plan tests the mechanism but never measures its blast radius on the live corpus.
findings.suggestion: Before wiring F11, run `evaluate_binding_completeness` in a dry-run over the current campaign corpus, count would-be-HARD FRs, and either (a) fix those bindings in the same diff, or (b) explicitly grandfather pre-rule FRs (e.g., only apply HARD to bindings touched/created after a cutoff). Record the dry-run numbers in the diff so the rollout risk is visible.  2. Category: approach — Severity: medium

findings.finding: The sub-iterate's own title and S3 text say "producers emit and require the binding," but this plan delivers only the require side (the enforcement check). The emit side — wiring into `/shipwright-project`, `/shipwright-adopt`, `/shipwright-iterate` — is deferred in the alternatives section, but the deferral has no tracked owner: no mention of updating the campaign card or SPEC to record which future sub-iterate picks it up. As written, P3.3 can close "done" while half its stated purpose silently falls through the cracks.
findings.suggestion: In the same diff, add one line to the campaign card (or SPEC Track V) noting that producer-side emission wiring is deferred to a named unit (P3.4/P3.6, whichever owns it), with the mini-plan's rationale.  3. Category: approach — Severity: medium

findings.finding: The plan says the new evaluator "mirrors `evaluate_cross_layer`'s ... hard/advisory severity routing" while sharing only the change-detection keys. A mirrored (copied) severity table in a separate module will drift from the original the first time someone adjusts severity rules in `_layer_coverage_core` — two gates that are supposed to make "one judgment by construction" will silently diverge.
findings.suggestion: Import or extract the severity routing into `_layer_coverage_core` (or a shared helper it already exposes) so both evaluators call the same code. If the mirror is truly copy-for-copy, the tests should at least assert parity on the shared cases.  4. Category: risk — Severity: low

findings.finding: A third independent "expensive regen-with-evidence" call per `run_all_checks` invocation, justified only by the precedent of the existing two. Precedent of duplicates isn't a cost argument — the new check is being added now and could share one regen snapshot with `check_cross_layer_coverage` within a single run.
findings.suggestion: At minimum, measure the added wall time before/after. Better: have `run_all_checks` produce the evidence snapshot once and pass it to both coverage checks in the same invocation. If the measurement shows negligible cost, the current approach is acceptable — but record that number.  5. Category: edge-case — Severity: medium

findings.finding: Layer rank ordering is tested for unit/integration/E2E, but there's no stated behavior for non-standard layer labels that may appear in coverage evidence (manual, static-analysis, perf, or any future label). Depending on implementation this either raises, silently skips, or mis-ranks.
findings.suggestion: Specify the behavior explicitly (ignore-with-advisory is probably right) and add a test for an unrecognized layer label in the evidence set.  6. Category: edge-case — Severity: medium

findings.finding: The ledger reconciliation method rests on the assumption "every post-Phase-2 (E) bullet already carries a trailing `(iterate-YYYY-MM-DD-…)` citation," verified against exactly two rows. If any post-Phase-2 bullet lacks a citation, has a malformed date, carries multiple citations, or sits under an FR whose walk-date heading was itself revised after the bullet was added, the "bullets the walk could not have seen" set is silently incomplete — and the resulting prose is documentation drift presented as reconciliation.
findings.suggestion: Mechanically enumerate all (E) bullets (grep) and assert each either has a parseable citation or provably predates Phase 2, before writing the prose section. This is cheap and turns a spot-check into a guarantee.  7. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: The second AC ("ledger rows and (E) bullets are reconciled") has no defined deliverable. The plan's method identifies un-walked bullets, but the AC could reasonably be read as requiring an explicit bullet→row mapping. If the reconciliation section ends up as narrative prose without a traceable mapping, the AC risks being judged unmet even though the work is sound.
findings.suggestion: Specify the section's contents in the plan: at minimum, a per-FR list of (E) bullets not covered by the walk, each with its citation date, plus a statement of the numbering-scheme relationship (per FR-01.18, not 1:1).  Security: No concerns — this is local compliance tooling reading repo files; no new inputs cross a trust boundary.  Over-production check: Passes. Two small focused modules, no new schema fields, no new dependencies, and the file split follows existing precedent rather than adding abstraction. The alternatives section correctly rejected a new JSON artifact and AC-level schema field.

findings.finding: The plan explicitly declines to wire producers, despite the change being titled and scoped as “Producers emit and require the binding.” A verifier that reads existing `required_layers` is only a consumer/enforcer; it does not ensure new or updated iterate/adopt/project outputs emit a complete binding.
findings.suggestion: Include the producer paths that create or update FR coverage/binding metadata, and make them populate or validate `required_layers` from the highest observable evidence layer. If that work truly belongs elsewhere, formally narrow and rename this sub-iterate before proceeding.

findings.finding: No authoritative rule is identified for deriving the “highest observable layer.” Reusing `coverage` fields assumes their layer labels are complete, normalized, and tied to the same FR/change, but the plan does not establish that contract.
findings.suggestion: Define the exact evidence eligibility and ranking inputs: accepted layer vocabulary, treatment of multiple evidence records, and whether only current/passing/change-relevant evidence counts. Add tests for unknown, malformed, and mixed-layer coverage.

findings.finding: A new hard gate in `run_all_checks` can block existing work if legacy detection is based only on source age or a broad “behavior changed” signal. A previously valid FR with stale or partial metadata may be unexpectedly classified as a new hard failure.
findings.suggestion: Specify and test the migration boundary precisely: existing records remain advisory, while newly produced or materially updated bindings are hard-failed. Ensure the diagnostic tells users which binding field and evidence item must be changed.

findings.finding: The planned tests omit the practical ambiguity cases: multiple higher layers, failed versus passing integration evidence, evidence for a different criterion, empty/unknown `required_layers`, and a declared layer higher than any observed evidence. These determine whether the check is trustworthy rather than noisy.
findings.suggestion: Add a compact parameterized test matrix covering those cases, including deterministic reporting of the expected highest required layer.

findings.finding: The ledger reconciliation is described as an investigation method, not a concrete reconciliation deliverable. Appending prose based on iterate-date citations may identify bullets a walk could not have seen, but it does not necessarily reconcile each ledger row to its corresponding `(E)` bullet or record intentional split/merge relationships.
findings.suggestion: Add a concise mapping table or exception list in the campaign document: each unreconciled `(E)` item, relevant ledger row(s), status, and rationale. State the resulting reconciliation outcome explicitly.

findings.finding: The plan accepts a third independent expensive regeneration call solely because two already exist. That preserves precedent but unnecessarily increases `run_all_checks` latency and creates another opportunity for inconsistent regenerated state between checks.
findings.suggestion: Reuse a single regenerated evidence snapshot within `run_all_checks` if the existing interfaces can accept it without introducing broad abstraction; otherwise document that each check operates on an immutable, deterministic source.  Overall, the evaluator is a plausible enforcement component, but the plan omits the producer work central to this change and leaves the highest-layer derivation contract underspecified. It needs those changes before it can demonstrate the requested end-to-end behavior.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: reject

findings.finding: The sub-iterate's scope is "Producers emit and require the binding." Only the require half (the F11 gate) is delivered; the emit half (wiring `/shipwright-project`, `/shipwright-adopt`, `/shipwright-iterate` to write complete bindings) is deferred to "P3.5 or a named follow-up card" — which is not guaranteed to exist. The deferral is documented and dispositioned, and the two literal acceptance criteria are arguably met, but the stated purpose of the unit is half-undelivered and the AC "binding must include the highest observable layer" is only enforced, never produced.
findings.suggestion: Either land a minimal producer change (even one of the three pipelines) in this unit, or get an explicit commitment recorded in campaign.md/SPEC naming the exact follow-up card id that owns emission — not "P3.5 or a follow-up."

findings.finding: When the only executed-passing layer is a non-canonical label, `_highest_ok_layer` returns that label (pinned by the test `{"manual": "ok"} == "manual"`), and the caller then computes `_LAYER_RANK.get(highest_ok, -1) <= max_required_rank`, which is `-1 <= -1` for an empty binding → `continue`, i.e. a non-canonical ok layer never triggers a gap even when `required_layers` is empty. This is defensible (fail-open on unknown vocabulary) but contradicts the docstring's fail-closed framing ("an unrecognised required layer must never be credited") — the evidence-side counterpart silently credits nothing. Low impact since coverage keys are canonical by construction; the behavior should at least be stated rather than emerge incidentally.
findings.suggestion: Either document this asymmetry in the module docstring or route an unknown ok-layer to an advisory when `required_layers` is empty.

findings.finding: This test only asserts the check's name appears in `run_all_checks` output on a bare tmp_path (skip path); it does not verify the check is actually wired into the enforcing list rather than e.g. filtered out, nor that a real gap would propagate to a failed `run_all_checks` result. A regression that removes the check from the list would fail it, but a regression that wires it with wrong arguments would not.
findings.suggestion: Add one end-to-end test where a behaviour-changed FR with unit-only binding and passing integration evidence causes `run_all_checks` to report a failure for this check name.

findings.finding: Both gap lists are truncated at 6 (`[:6]`) with no "+N more" indicator, and the count in the message (`len(verdict.hard)`) can exceed the items shown, which may confuse triage. Cosmetic-but-real reporting gap.
findings.suggestion: Append a `(+N more)` suffix when truncated.

findings.finding: The change explicitly defers the producer “emit” half, despite this sub-iterate being scoped as “Producers emit and require the binding.” The new gate only consumes existing `required_layers`; new or updated producer outputs can still omit or understate that binding until some later, unspecified implementation.
findings.suggestion: Wire the project/adopt/iterate producer paths to emit or update the binding based on qualifying evidence, or formally narrow the specification before accepting this change.

findings.finding: The evaluator treats a binding that declares a higher layer as complete even when it does not name the highest observed layer. For example, `required_layers=["e2e"]` with executed-passing `integration` evidence passes, although the binding does not include `integration`; a future integration regression is therefore not required by the binding. This contradicts “must include the highest observable layer.”
findings.suggestion: Require the actual highest passing canonical layer to be present in `required_layers`, rather than comparing only ranks. Update the test that currently asserts a higher declared layer is clean.

findings.finding: The wrapper’s full-path test only exercises a clean manifest. The primary rejection behavior is tested in the pure evaluator and result formatter separately, so a wrapper regression that supplies the wrong manifests or fails to propagate an evaluator gap would still pass the wrapper-path tests.
findings.suggestion: Add a full wrapper-path test with a behavior-changed unit-only binding and passing integration/e2e evidence, asserting a non-skipped hard-failure `CheckResult`.  Overall: ship-with-fixes. The gate largely implements the require-side acceptance criterion, but the stated producer work is absent and the rank-only comparison weakens the highest-layer requirement.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
